items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Public methods have one-line docs, but internals of durability.go (durabilityManager fields, minRetainedJobID logic, notifyWaitersLocked) have no comments. DurabilityStats fields are undocumented. onBatchDurable takes 8 positional args. Hacky reflect.Pointer comparison is unexplained.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The type is properly isolated in durability.go, but notifyWaitersLocked duplicates the same isDurable/firstErr/closed branches for seqWaiters and subscriptions, and the ctx.Done branches are copied too. The commit.go error paths are dead code: `b.db = nil` runs before `if syncWAL && b.db != nil`.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The failure callback on prepare/apply errors never fires because b.db is nilled first, so the 'even on failure' requirement is silently dropped. The NoSyncWait goroutine reads b.fsyncWait/b.commitErr after Commit returns, which races with batch reuse. Magic 10000 limits. Expired/unknown logic breaks on shared job IDs (hidden test fails).

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API is additive, but every sync commit takes the durabilityManager mutex even when BatchDurable is unset. NoSyncWait commits now spawn a goroutine per commit. When BatchDurable is configured, d.newJobID() (under d.mu) runs per commit and shifts the job IDs seen by flush/compaction events.
